ratings_why.fun: Choosing which carry to hang three climbers on and watching the vines rise is a real draft, but early turns are thin and the tribe needs a good host from another tribe.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7: it's the only tribe whose payoff is another tribe's carry, and it makes the back row and board arrangement the main decision, which no tribe today does.

verdict_why: The cards read cleanly and the fantasy shows in what they do; what's left is screen work (vines, gain tracking) and small wording, not design.

points.text: Rise depends on each host's biggest gain this round, which a player can't see on the board. Show that number on each host next to the vine, or the tribe's main rule stays invisible.
Woodbine's 'never given to that unit before' is hidden memory. Mark flattered units (a pressed flower on the card) so the shuffle reads at a glance.
Barley-Sugar Twiner says 'its host gains its biggest gain'; writing 'its host repeats the host's biggest gain this round' removes the double 'its'.
Apple Mistletoe's 'attacks ignore Shield' is a nice nod to Baldr's oath, but nothing on the card tells a player why; it reads as a stray rider.
Young Ivy turning into Adult Ivy is the clearest growing-up moment in the tribe; show the 3-gain count as leaves on the card.

standouts.why: Lady Hedera's guest-book is the fantasy as a rule: you move her from patron to patron to collect tribes, and the payoff is plain.
Viscum only climbs the biggest unit and loses his host if he outgrows it; the snob's limit is the card's rule.
Young Ivy grows into Adult Ivy as it climbs, just like real ivy reaching the light, and it is easy to read.

weakest.why: Ivy-clad Ruin's sideways climbing is a rules patch more than a ruin held up by ivy, and its golden does a different job.
Dodder Seedling is a plain Attack skim; nothing in it says 'find a host fast'.
Traveller's Joy is the longest text in the tribe for a half-share fight echo, and it needs a disclaimer to keep it from chaining.

flags.note: Viscum copies every gain in full; on an Ooze that eats, or on Cousin Dodder, that is a very large number each turn.
Cousin Dodder keeps a quarter of the biggest enemy every attack, permanently, and climbers rise with it.
